$comparability.why: This file was measured against the previous golden set, which is not a golden set: 33 of its 100 protocols are not what the published stratified rule produces from the committed 159-document corpus, 95 of 95 protocols had drifted, 0 of 260 rules carried a snapshot id or a character offset, and 10 probes were unreachable in the section they named. node eval/build-golden.mjs did not reproduce it. These numbers are NOT comparable to any run made against eval/golden.json.
what_changed_in_the_instrument: RECALL is now reported under a BOUNDED matcher (the emitted row may not exceed the probe by more than 1.5x) beside the containment matcher that was used here; both are in every new results file.
RECALL is now reported beside its own FLOOR (three deliberately trivial extractors) and marked VOID where the floor beats it.
VERIFY is now one number per verdict condition, not one pooled percentage of the store against itself.
CALLS is now over three divisors, with the harness auditing calls separated from the calls a caller pays.
NEGATIVE PROBES and CONSERVATION are new; neither has a counterpart in this file.
$comparability.supersedes_note: Nothing in this file is wrong about the build it measured. It is simply measured against a set that cannot be rebuilt, and a number without a rebuildable denominator is an anecdote with decimals.

RECALL.headline_rule: strict and weak are never added together; keyword-free is reported apart because no keyword-driven extractor can reach it.

CALLS.note: Every tools.rfc.* call the harness makes for the golden set: 1 resolve to pin each snapshot, 1 scoped requirements per protocol, 1 unscoped requirements per protocol to measure what a caller pays without a section hint, extra pages when a section exceeds the 200-row ceiling, and 1-2 verify_citation per matched rule. Corpus invariants are a separate instrument over all 151 documents and are excluded from this number.
